blues (musical genre of African American origin)

Borrowed from English capsaicin, alteration of earlier capsicine.
Borrowed from English catamaran, from Tamil கட்டுமரம் (kaṭṭumaram).

parole.significato: Death Eater (A member of the group of dark wizards led by Voldemort in the Harry Potter series.)
parole.testo: From cavaller (“knight”) + de (“of”) + la (“the”) + mort (“death”), literally “knight of death,” coined for the Catalan translations of the Harry Potter series as a semantic adaptation of English Death Eater.

parole.significato: cent (a hundredth of a half step)
parole.testo: Borrowed from English cent. These senses of the word cent in Catalan derive from the inversion of meaning that took place in English where it was used to indicate one hundredth.
Partial calque of English cyberpunk. Equivalent to ciber- + punk.
Borrowed from English clan, from Irish and Scottish Gaelic clann.

parole.significato: club (an association of members joining together for some common purpose, especially sports or recreation)

parole.testo: Borrowed from English cola, in turn from an undetermined Niger-Congo language, compare Temne kola, Mandinka kola.

From cripto- + moneda. Calque of English cryptocurrency.
Borrowed from English cross. The sense "cross country" is a pseudo-anglicism, derived from English cross country. -cross exists in English to refer to cross country, but only as a suffix.

parole.significato: cryptid (creature who existence has not been scientifically confirmed)
parole.testo: Borrowed from English cryptid. By surface analysis, cript- + -id.

Borrowed from English camera, from New Latin camera obscura (“dark chamber”), from Latin camera (“chamber, bedchamber”). Doublet of the inherited cambra.

Borrowed from English dollar, from Dutch daalder, from German Thaler.

parole.significato: Irish (pertaining to Irish or the Irish language)
parole.testo: Borrowed from English Gaelic, ultimately from Old Irish Goídel (“Gael”).

Borrowed from English glamorous. Equivalent to glamur + -ós.

parole.significato: Goidelic (pertaining to the Goidels or the Goidelic languages)
parole.testo: Borrowed from English Goidelic, from Old Irish Goídel (“Gael”) + -ic. As with English, this term is used to avoid the ambiguity associated with the term gaèlic (“Gaelic”).

From English hydrant, probably via French.
From hiper- + text. Calque of English hypertext.
Borrowed from English homophobia. By surface analysis, homo- + -fòbia.

parole.significato: Malay (pertaining to the Malay Peninsula, to the Malay people, or to the Malay language)
